correctness.rationale: The ring is the projective edge semigroup algebra, not the edge ideal. The cube bipartition has 4+4 vertices, hence the incidence-polytope affine span has rank 6, and deleting one coordinate in each class gives its full Z^6 lattice; the gcd of the 6x6 minors of differences is one. Total unimodularity of signed bipartite incidence guarantees the integer-decomposition property and ring normality over any field. A fresh independent exact-integer program enumerated 924 affinely spanning six-subsets, found 12 primitive facet inequalities and all 349 faces with f-vector (12,54,110,108,52,12,1), recomputed primitive normal rays and all maximal cone minor gcds; exactly 50 nonregular faces occur by dimensions 0,1,2 as 12,30,8, and every nonregular cone is nonsimplicial. The inclusion-maximal nonregular faces are exactly the 8 star triangles and 6 antipodal edge-pairs. The toric orbit-face correspondence identifies their orbit closures as coordinate P^2 and P^1 because those face monomials are affinely independent. Their intersections lie at the 12 coordinate points, each on 3 components, yielding 36 intersecting component pairs. Stanley--Reisner union face counts (12,30,8) imply the displayed rational Hilbert series and for n>=1 the Hilbert function 12+30(n-1)+8 C(n-1,2)=4n^2+18n-10; Hilbert polynomial thus holds in any characteristic. Singular locus is reduced support only; non-Q-factorial locus matches because all simplicial cones are regular. The independent checker is finite exhaustive for this fixed polytope; normality, toric smoothness and face-orbit principles are separate mathematical arguments, not merely VERIFY_OK.
residual_risks: The nonreduced Jacobian singular scheme and completed transverse local analytic types are not claimed.
Only Q3 and its exact 349-face fan are certified; no claim for higher hypercubes or arbitrary crown graphs.

originality.rationale: The precise novel candidate is the complete reduced singular-orbit support of the projective edge toric variety of Q3, equivalently the 4x4 crown graph/diagonal-deleted Segre parametrization, and its coordinate-union Hilbert function. Primary Ohsugi--Hibi results prove normality and characterize global simplicity/smoothness but stop short of locating the eight maximal star-triangle singular orbits and six incomparable antipodal-pair orbits. Kahle et al. describe partial-rank-one completability and its algebraic constraints, not this projective normal-fan singular support. Resultary searches for cube, crown, off-diagonal Segre and exact Hilbert data found related but different published claims. The general toric orbit criterion plus a new exhaustive face computation yields this particular classification. One plausible 2021 affine bipartite graph rigidity source remains full-text inaccessible, leaving a real but not decisive priority risk.
residual_risks: The 2021 Portakal affine bipartite-graph rigidity paper could contain a relevant hidden general-face classification; original full text was inaccessible due institutional VPN disconnection, not treated as disproof of novelty.

value.rationale: The smallest cubic hypercube Q3 and the crown graph K4,4 minus a matching are canonical objects, and their projective edge ring is a natural sparse rank-one matrix projection. A complete classification of all maximal singular toric-orbit closures is a genuinely motivated exact structural invariant: the singular reduced support is nonpure with eight surface components and six additional curve components, not merely globally singular. The explicit incidence pattern and Hilbert series quantify geometry that cannot be inferred from normality or the ambient variety Hilbert polynomial alone. The singularity support is finite-dimensional but not an arbitrary unmotivated slice; it is the full classification for this natural sixfold. No unsupported claims about larger graph families or nonreduced schemes are used.
residual_risks: One explicit small graph computation may have narrow transfer beyond sparse Segre toric geometry; value resides in the complete natural-case classification rather than an asserted general theorem.

limitations: Full nonreduced singular scheme, transverse local analytic types and higher hypercube cases are not asserted.
